subject: Inference readiness and JSON-output compliance — next steps
messages:
From: Tom Granger <tom.granger@heliosanalytics.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aisha Patel <aisha@heliosanalytics.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jan 2029 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quick follow-up + sample data (post-demo)

Hi Karthik — thanks again for the demo today. Appreciate the walkthrough of routing/fallbacks and the live example of structured outputs.

Attaching a small sample of our canonical output rows and one of the JSON schema variants we currently try to validate against. Our immediate priorities are:
- reliably producing a fixed JSON object for downstream ingestion (strict keys, types)
- stable quality across our critical LTV prompts (fewer hallucinations)
- an approach to retries/backoff when the model returns partial schema or type mismatches

Files attached: model-benchmark-run-20290110.csv (sample inference logs), sample-prompt-set-v1.json (10 canonical prompts), example-output-schema-v2.json (their schema).

Questions:
1) Which model variants should we attempt first for cost/latency tradeoffs?
2) What does Redwood recommend for JSON schema enforcement at request time vs. post-processing?
3) Any suggested retry/backoff policy you’ve seen work well when the model produces invalid JSON?

Tom
Product Lead, Helios Analytics

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Granger <tom.granger@heliosanalytics.com>
Cc: Aisha Patel <aisha@heliosanalytics.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: Quick follow-up + sample data (post-demo)

Tom — great to get the sample artifacts, thanks. Recapping next steps and a pragmatic plan so we’re aligned. High level recommendations below (short, actionable):

1) Model suggestions (fast experiments)
- Redwood-1-small (quantized): start here for low latency and predictable token cost. Good for structured-output tasks where prompt engineering is tight.
- LlamaX-8Q (8-bit): middle ground if you need slightly better factuality at modest latency cost.
- Redwood-2-medium: recommend only if initial runs show quality regressions you can’t fix with prompt/schema constraints.

2) Benchmarks we’ll run (we’ll run these and share results)
- Gold-set pass rate: run your 120 canonical prompts vs. each model, measure schema-valid JSON pass (strict key/type), token cost, p95 latency.
- Quality regression checks: BLEU/ROUGE-style automated diff against expected key values + a small human-annotated sample (50 examples) for hallucination scoring.

3) JSON enforcement strategy (pragmatic + robust)
- Request-time validation: use streaming with schema-aware decoding hooks we provide. If the stream violates schema, we can auto-abort and return an explicit error code so the caller can fallback.
- Post-process validation: always run a strict validator as second line; log reasons for failure for our eval dashboards.
- Hybrid: allow relaxed parsing for tolerant routes (analytics) and strict enforcement for ingestion routes (ETL).

4) Retry / backoff policy (what we recommend)
- Immediate numeric type coercion: 1 quick retry with a small correction prompt when only minor type mismatches detected.
- Structured-failure: if the response is non-JSON or missing required keys, do exponential backoff with jitter: retry up to 3 times (0.5s, 1.5s, 4s) with a short repair prompt that urges the model to return only valid JSON.
- Circuit breaker: if %failures for a route > 5% in 10 minutes, route to a cheaper deterministic fallback or prefilled cached result while we investigate.

5) Deliverables and owners
- Redwood: run the first benchmarking sweep (Redwood-1-small, LlamaX-8Q) against your sample prompts, deliver CSV of results + pass/fail counts (owner: Neha).
- Helios: share the 50 human-annotated examples for hallucination scoring (owner: Aisha).
- Redwood: provide a suggested streaming-decoder snippet + a quick post-processing validator you can drop into your ingestion pipeline (owner: Vanessa).

Proposed next meeting: Tue 16 Jan 2029, 9am PT — quick 30m to review benchmark outputs and decide the canary route. Does that work?

I’ll attach a short playbook draft and the links to the eval runner once Neha kicks off the job.

Thanks — Karthik
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: inference-playbook-proposal-Helios.pdf (application/pdf)]

Date: Sat, 12 Jan 2029 08:02:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Quick follow-up + sample data (post-demo)

Thanks — the plan looks good. A couple of clarifications from our side before you run the sweep: 
- Our ingestion pipeline expects strict types (ints, strings, nested arrays). We cannot accept numeric-as-strings.
- Some prompts include private PII fields (hashed IDs). We need to understand the best path for encryption-at-rest and audit logs for inference calls. SOC2 + audit logs are a hard requirement.

Also, re: retries — we want to avoid materially increasing cost by retrying too often. The circuit-breaker approach sounds sensible; can you include a cost estimate for the 3x retry path vs. the 1x path?

Finally — can you attach an initial prompt-set variant (we’ll run it in parallel) that biases the model to prefer terse, strictly-typed outputs?

Appreciate it,
Aisha
Sr. ML Engineer, Helios Analytics
From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Jan 2029 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Helios benchmarking kickoff — action items

Looping internal owners — quick internal note to confirm responsibilities and timeline. Posting Karthik's plan here and adding operational details.

Action items (owners & ETA):
- Neha: start the benchmark sweep now (Redwood-1-small, LlamaX-8Q). Deliverables: results CSV, per-prompt pass rate, per-model p95 latency. ETA: Mon 2029-01-15 EOD.
- Vanessa: draft the streaming-decoder snippet + a JSON validation library example targeted at their example-output-schema-v2.json. Also include a 3-retry backoff snippet and a cost delta table. ETA: Tue 2029-01-16.
- Marissa: prepare the human-annotation sampling template and instructions for Helios to annotate 50 examples. Also include a quick rubric for hallucination scoring. ETA: Tue 2029-01-16.
- Karthik: confirm 16 Jan meeting (we're tentatively holding 9am PT). Reach out to Helios to confirm SOC2 & audit-log contract questions; loop legal if they need an enterprise addendum.

Notes: keep the benchmark runs to a small concurrency to avoid noisy p95 spikes. Use prefix-caching disabled so we capture cold-start behavior for their prompts. Attachments referenced: sample-prompt-set-v1.json (from Helios).

I’ll create a shared drive folder and post the benchmark CSV and the draft snippet there.

— Neha
Product Reliability, Redwood Inference
